# Decides WHICH RACE a child of mixed parentage is. It does not decide what the child looks like:
# that is gfx/portraits/portrait_modifiers/99_gen_race_morphs.txt (a generated file — see
# Emit/RaceMorphWriter.cs), which forces the race-defining genes by trait at render time while
# everything else — nose, eyes, mouth, cheeks, hair, colouring — blends from the parents normally.
#
# History of this file, because the failure mode is worth remembering: an earlier version ran
# `copy_inheritable_appearance_from` on EVERY birth in the game, unguarded. On a human map that made
# every child a genetic near-clone of one randomly chosen parent, flattening family variation
# world-wide; inside a race it made siblings identical; and it copied whole genomes across sexes,
# which vanilla itself only ever does behind a `sex_same_as` check. Dropping the genome copy — and
# letting the portrait modifier carry the race instead — fixes all three at once, and covers the
# engine-generated characters the birth hook can never see.

gen_resolve_child_phenotype_effect = {
	# Nothing to decide unless a race is actually in play — including the human race, which on a
	# fantasy map is a trait like any other, so a child of two humans is settled here at birth
	# rather than waiting for the culture pulse. A truly untagged parent pair (pre-pulse engine
	# characters) still falls through at the cost of one trigger per birth. (This file only ships
	# on fantasy maps — see Emit/StaticFileWriter.cs.)
	if = {
		limit = {
			OR = {
				mother ?= { gen_has_phenotype_trigger = yes }
				real_father ?= { gen_has_phenotype_trigger = yes }
			}
		}

		# One parent is chosen and the child takes their race whole. When both parents are the same
		# race the coin flip is a no-op, so it needs no special case; when one is human the child
		# has an even chance of coming out human, which is what makes a mixed line thin out over
		# generations instead of every descendant staying fantastical.
		if = {
			limit = {
				exists = mother
				exists = real_father
			}
			random_list = {
				50 = { gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = mother } }
				50 = { gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = real_father } }
			}
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = { exists = mother }
			gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = mother }
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = { exists = real_father }
			gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = real_father }
		}
	}

	gen_resolve_half_race_effect = yes

	# Horns, once the race is known: Hornborn for a child of the horned people who came out of
	# another race, and a fallback horn style for anyone owed horns (00_horn_effects.txt).
	gen_resolve_hornborn_effect = yes
	gen_assign_horn_style_effect = yes
}

# Half-elves and half-orcs. Runs after the race is decided, and only marks a child who came out HUMAN:
# a child who took the elf or orc parent's race is simply that race, full features and all.
#
# A human child is half-elf when a parent is an elf, or when BOTH parents are half-elves. A half-elf
# with a plain human has plain human children — the half features are not passed on — and a
# half-elf with a full elf either rolls elf or rolls human with an elf parent, which is half-elf
# again. The same for orcs.
#
# The flags carry the LOOK only: gfx/portraits/portrait_modifiers/99_gen_race_morphs.txt (generated,
# see Emit/RaceMorphWriter.cs) gives gen_half_elf half-strength pointed ears and gen_half_orc
# half-grown tusks, and clears inherited ears and tusks on every other human of a mixed line. Race
# is still one trait, so nothing else in the phenotype system needs to know half-races exist.
gen_resolve_half_race_effect = {
	if = {
		limit = { has_trait = phenotype_human }
		if = {
			limit = {
				OR = {
					mother ?= { gen_is_elf_phenotype_trigger = yes }
					real_father ?= { gen_is_elf_phenotype_trigger = yes }
					AND = {
						mother ?= { has_character_flag = gen_half_elf }
						real_father ?= { has_character_flag = gen_half_elf }
					}
				}
			}
			add_character_flag = gen_half_elf
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = {
				OR = {
					mother ?= { has_trait = phenotype_rough_hewn }
					real_father ?= { has_trait = phenotype_rough_hewn }
					AND = {
						mother ?= { has_character_flag = gen_half_orc }
						real_father ?= { has_character_flag = gen_half_orc }
					}
				}
			}
			add_character_flag = gen_half_orc
		}
	}
}

# Half-races for the HISTORY cast, once, at game start (gen_phenotype_game_start_on_action).
#
# History characters are never born in game, so gen_resolve_half_race_effect above never saw them:
# a human whose father was a minority elf in a human culture carried the ears in DNA and no flag.
# Same rule as at birth — a human with an elf (orc) parent is half-elf (half-orc) — but the parents
# are read by genome as well as trait, because a parent dead before the bookmark was never
# reconciled and still wears the culture's phenotype_human.
#
# Deliberately left out: the "both parents half" case. Dead parents are never flagged, and living
# ones may not be flagged yet in the same sweep, so it would answer by iteration order. Births from
# here on apply it as usual.
gen_resolve_history_half_race_effect = {
	if = {
		limit = {
			has_trait = phenotype_human
			NOT = { has_character_flag = gen_half_elf }
			NOT = { has_character_flag = gen_half_orc }
		}
		if = {
			limit = {
				OR = {
					mother ?= { gen_is_elf_blooded_trigger = yes }
					real_father ?= { gen_is_elf_blooded_trigger = yes }
				}
			}
			add_character_flag = gen_half_elf
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = {
				OR = {
					mother ?= { gen_is_orc_blooded_trigger = yes }
					real_father ?= { gen_is_orc_blooded_trigger = yes }
				}
			}
			add_character_flag = gen_half_orc
		}
	}
}

# Copies one parent's race onto the newborn.
#
# Written as an else_if chain rather than seven independent ifs so a parent who somehow carries two
# phenotypes — the `opposites` lists are meant to prevent it, but the ruler designer and the console
# can still produce one — hands over exactly one instead of stacking them onto the child.
gen_take_parent_race_effect = {
	$PARENT$ = { save_scope_as = gen_race_donor }

	if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_gracile } }
		add_trait = phenotype_gracile
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_sylvan } }
		add_trait = phenotype_sylvan
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_stocky } }
		add_trait = phenotype_stocky
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_rough_hewn } }
		add_trait = phenotype_rough_hewn
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_towering } }
		add_trait = phenotype_towering
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_diminutive } }
		add_trait = phenotype_diminutive
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_dusk_adapted } }
		add_trait = phenotype_dusk_adapted
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_horned } }
		add_trait = phenotype_horned
	}
	else = {
		# The chosen donor is human. Say so explicitly: an unmarked child is indistinguishable from
		# one the birth hook never reached, and the yearly pulse would hand it the local culture's
		# race — overruling the parents, which is the one thing that must always win at birth.
		add_trait = phenotype_human

		# The mixed-line flag rides along only when this bloodline actually touches a fantasy race:
		# a parent who is fantasy-traited (this birth is the mixed one), or a parent already flagged
		# (the mix is further up the line — gen_race_skin is inheritable, so an elven skin shift can
		# resurface generations later and the render-time reset must keep following the line).
		# Two plain-human parents — which since the human trait spread broadly includes every
		# minority-race couple — set no flag, and that is load-bearing: minority members LOOK their
		# race through rolled ethnicity genes while counting as human, and the flag would snap their
		# skin back to the human template at render (see gen_race_skin_human in the generated
		# 99_gen_race_morphs.txt).
		if = {
			limit = {
				OR = {
					mother ?= {
						OR = {
							gen_has_fantasy_phenotype_trigger = yes
							has_character_flag = gen_phenotype_human
						}
					}
					real_father ?= {
						OR = {
							gen_has_fantasy_phenotype_trigger = yes
							has_character_flag = gen_phenotype_human
						}
					}
				}
			}
			add_character_flag = gen_phenotype_human
		}
	}

	# A minority's child is a minority too. gen_phenotype_from_gene marks a character whose race is
	# NOT their culture's, and gen_assign_phenotype_effect refuses such a culture head as the template
	# for the culture's engine-generated courtiers. The flag used to stop at the first generation:
	# a gnome born to the gnomes seated among a human people took the trait here but not the flag, so
	# if that child later became the culture's head, every courtier the engine invented for the
	# culture copied phenotype_diminutive — and the portrait modifier then forced gnome bodies onto
	# them. Riding along with the race closes it. Only when the child actually took the donor's
	# fantasy race: a human child of a minority parent is its culture's race and must stay eligible.
	if = {
		limit = {
			gen_has_fantasy_phenotype_trigger = yes
			scope:gen_race_donor = { has_character_flag = gen_phenotype_from_gene }
		}
		add_character_flag = gen_phenotype_from_gene
	}
}
